author: Lynch, John
title: Low vowel dissimilation in Vanuatu languages
notes: Consulted directly on 23 November 2026 (Project MUSE PDF, text layer). Low vowel dissimilation (lvd): the first *a of *aCa raised to ə, later e (or i, o, zero), left to right in most languages, blocked by velars, postvelars and labiovelars; Lynch proposes one dissimilation in the ancestor of the languages from Malakula and Ambrym to Aneityum, with later reversal (ə > a) in the languages that do not show it (§5). Entered for the lects in the data: Paamese, Southeast Ambrym, Vinmavis (Neve'ei), South Efate and Proto-Southern Vanuatu. Not entered: the many Malakula languages known from Charpentier (1982) (Table 1, Table 2), the productive rules (§3), Marshallese and Woleaian (§6, no reconstruction stated against their parents).
